title: End-to-end tests for Dedicated staged rollouts (workflow + flaky-signal simulations)
creator: Leila Farouk
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
sub_issues: ENG-5995.1 Add rollout plan happy-path e2e (create -> promote -> complete)
ENG-5995.3 Add flaky/missing telemetry simulations + assertions on semantics
ENG-5995.4 Add multi-region impairment test (partial region down mid-stage)
content:
Overview
We need automated end-to-end validation for the Dedicated staged rollouts workflow:
- create rollout plan
- start rollout
- promote through stages
- simulate gate failures (hard fail + missing/flaky signals)
- validate abort/rollback semantics (traffic split reversal, state machine, audit events)

This ticket focuses on QA automation and reproducible simulations. These tests are a GA launch requirement and will run in CI on every release train for the control plane + routing + policy engine.

Background / references
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-staged-rollouts-reserved-pools-prd.json
- Confluence design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/staged-rollouts-for-dedicated-pools-design-spec.json
- ADRs: stage model, gate signals/thresholds, rollback semantics
- Routing + gate work is landing in parallel (ENG-5941 / ENG-5950). Telemetry tagging is required for stage-aware queries (ENG-5966).

Goals
1) Validate the critical operator workflow is safe and reversible:
   - Create plan with default stages (1/10/50/100) and gates
   - Promote stage-by-stage
   - Automatic abort/rollback when gates fail
   - Hold/force-promote paths are covered at least minimally (smoke level)

2) Validate correctness under flakiness:
   - missing metrics (telemetry lag/outage)
   - delayed metrics (stale windows)
   - noisy/bursty traffic creating borderline gates

3) Ensure determinism:
   - idempotency keys for promote/abort are honored under retries
   - optimistic concurrency: double-promote cannot advance two stages

Non-goals
- Performance benchmarking or load testing at scale (handled by perf suite and SRE load tests)
- Exhaustive UI testing (Console team has separate contract tests; we focus on API + routing outcomes)

Test environment / harness
- Use the simulated Dedicated pool harness introduced for rollout testing (test-only control plane + routing sandbox).
- Run against:
  - dedicated-pool-rollouts service (control plane)
  - policy engine gate evaluator
  - routing layer stage splitter
  - telemetry stub / fake metrics backend with programmable behaviors
- Emit/verify audit events for create/promote/abort/override actions.

Implementation plan
A. Core e2e cases (must have)
1) Happy path: create plan -> start -> promote 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% -> completed
   Assertions:
   - rollout state transitions: draft -> running -> completed
   - stage current_stage is updated exactly once per promotion
   - routing split matches stage definition (traffic or replica partition, per final stage model)
   - gate evidence snapshot exists per stage evaluation
   - audit events recorded with actor + stage + reason

2) Gate failure triggers rollback
   - Induce elevated error_rate or p99 latency in canary partition
   - Expect gate status FAIL -> rollout abort semantics applied
   Assertions:
   - state transitions: running -> aborted (or running -> aborting -> aborted if intermediate is implemented)
   - traffic split reverts to last known-good stage (typically prior stage, or 0% new if failing at first stage)
   - in-flight streaming behavior: requests already assigned remain pinned; new requests route to stable partition (verify via request tags)
   - audit event includes failure reason and gate that failed

3) Idempotency + retry safety
   - Send promote requests with same idempotency key under simulated retry (duplicate HTTP requests)
   - Assert stage only advances once
   - Assert second request returns same outcome with safe response

B. Flaky-signal simulations
4) Missing telemetry (policy decision: fail-closed with manual override)
   - Make gate query backend return NO_DATA / stale beyond threshold for the evaluation window
   - Expect gate status UNKNOWN -> treated as FAIL for auto-promotion (promotion blocked)
   - Assert rollout remains in held state (or running-but-blocked depending on final state machine)
   - Assert evidence shows staleness reason (explicitly surfaced for Console)

5) Telemetry lag causing late-arriving bad signals
   - Provide initially passing metrics; promote to next stage
   - After promotion, inject delayed metrics for the previous window that would have failed
   - Assert we do NOT retroactively abort the already-promoted stage unless the current window fails (per determinism requirement)
   - Add note: if product decides retroactive abort is required, update tests accordingly (flagged as open question in design spec)

6) Noisy metrics around threshold
   - Generate jitter around p95/p99
   - Validate minimum sample size logic (if implemented) and that gate evaluator uses aggregation window + hysteresis as specified in ADR

C. Multi-region impairment (nice-to-have, but strongly recommended)
7) Region impairment mid-stage
   - Two-region dedicated pool
   - During 10% stage, disable capacity in one region or make it unhealthy
   - Assert routing policy + fallback behavior:
     - does not starve remaining region
     - respects guardrails against over-partitioning
     - stage dashboard attribution remains correct (this is mostly telemetry tagging correctness)

Acceptance criteria
- Tests run in CI and are stable (flake rate < 1% across 50 runs).
- CI runtime budget: <= 12 minutes for the suite.
- Clear failure messages pointing to the broken component (control plane vs routing vs telemetry vs policy engine).
- Tests validate audit events are emitted for promote/abort (basic schema fields).

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: tests become brittle due to dynamic thresholds or default gate changes.
  Mitigation: freeze test gate thresholds explicitly in test plan payloads; avoid relying on global defaults.

- Risk: telemetry cardinality changes break tag-based assertions.
  Mitigation: assert only allowlisted tags (pool_id, rollout_id, stage_id, region) and avoid per-request high-cardinality labels.

- Risk: state machine changes (held/aborting states) invalidate assertions.
  Mitigation: assert on invariants (no stage skipping; no split mismatch; abort results in stable routing) + allow small set of acceptable intermediate states.

Links
- Feature implementation PRs (dependencies):
  - DB model + migrations: sources/github/redwood/pr-28411-add-dedicated-rollout-plan-model-and-migrations.json
  - CRUD + validation: sources/github/redwood/pr-28437-control-plane-rollout-plan-crud-and-validation.json
  - Promote/abort + audit: sources/github/redwood/pr-28458-implement-promote-abort-actions-with-audit-events.json
  - Gate eval v1: sources/github/redwood/pr-28476-policy-engine-gate-evaluation-v1.json
  - Routing split by stage: sources/github/redwood/pr-28503-routing-split-by-stage-for-dedicated-pools.json
  - Telemetry stage tags: sources/github/redwood/pr-28521-emit-stage-tags-in-metrics-and-traces.json

Progress updates
- 2025-02-14 (Leila Farouk): Created initial test skeleton and harness wiring. Blocked on stable promote/abort semantics landing (ENG-5941) and routing stage selection (ENG-5950).
- 2025-02-21 (Leila Farouk): Added happy-path e2e with fake telemetry backend. Noted mismatch between stage_id tag name in metrics vs traces; leaving assertion flexible until ENG-5966 finalizes tag allowlist.
- 2025-02-26 (Leila Farouk): Implemented gate-fail test using injected error_rate spike in canary partition. Observed occasional nondeterminism due to evaluator window boundary; aligned test clock with evaluator window start and added fixed time control.
- 2025-03-03 (Leila Farouk): Added missing-telemetry simulation. Confirmed policy is fail-closed for auto-promotion; tests assert promotion is blocked and rollout can be held pending manual override.
- 2025-03-06 (Leila Farouk): Added idempotency duplicate-promote test. Found bug: second promote with same idempotency key sometimes returned 409 instead of replaying result; filed follow-up for Platform (Jordan Lee) and temporarily asserted acceptable 200/409 with no state change.
- 2025-03-10 (Leila Farouk): Landed suite in main and enabled in CI nightly + release branch gating. Routed a dashboard link in CI output to speed triage.

Outcome / resolution
Implemented end-to-end integration tests for Dedicated staged rollouts, including:
- create plan -> promote -> complete
- gate fail -> abort/rollback routing
- missing telemetry / flaky-signal behavior
- idempotency protection under retries

Merged via: sources/github/redwood/pr-28610-integration-tests-staged-rollouts-dedicated.json

Follow-ups
- ENG-XXXX: tighten idempotency replay response (avoid 409 on duplicate idempotency key; prefer replayed 200 with same action_id).
- ENG-XXXX: add multi-region impairment test once region-routing policy stabilizes (depends on final behavior from routing team).
- Update runbooks to reference CI suite + how to reproduce locally (coordinate with Connor O'Brien + Elliot Price).
